title: Two drinks from one bottle
prompt: A bottle contains 84 mL of water. Jack drinks a third of it, then a quarter of what is left. How many millilitres remain?

title: A seed store works backwards
prompt: A seed store gives half its seeds to one garden, then a third of the remaining seeds to another. It has 30 seeds left. How many seeds did it start with?

title: Find the whole from the extra parts
prompt: A mixture has oats and seeds in the ratio 5 to 3 by weight. It contains 14 grams more oats than seeds. How many grams of mixture are there?

title: One paint colour catches up
prompt: Blue and white paints are mixed in the ratio 2 to 5. There are 14 mL of blue in the mixture. How many millilitres of blue must be added to make the amounts of blue and white equal?

title: Discount and delivery
prompt: A kit marked at $140 is discounted by 25%. Delivery costs $7 and is charged after the discount. What is the delivered cost in dollars?

title: The percentage on the way back
prompt: A club's membership grows from 56 to 70. By what percentage of the new membership must it decrease to get back to 56? Enter the percentage as a number.

title: How many travel a different way?
prompt: In one group of 42 children, one-third cycle to school. In another group of 28 children, one-half cycle. How many children in the two groups do not cycle?

title: Use the full bottle count
prompt: A crate contains 21 glass bottles and 14 metal bottles. One-third of the glass bottles and half the metal bottles are empty. What fraction of all the bottles are full? Give an exact fraction.

title: Compare the two prices
prompt: A bag is marked $60. The shop reduces the price by 20%. A second shop sells it for $49 with no additional charges. How many dollars cheaper is the discounted bag at the first shop?

title: A price after two changes
prompt: A bike light is reduced by 25%. A week later the reduced price is increased by 20%. The final price is $54. What was the price before either change, in dollars?

title: Three trays make one fraction
prompt: Three trays hold 8, 12 and 16 muffins. Half of the first tray's muffins, a third of the second's, and a quarter of the third's are chocolate. What fraction of all the muffins are chocolate?

title: Two classes of equal size
prompt: Two classes have equal numbers of pupils. Three-quarters of the first class and one-third of the second class wear glasses. Altogether 13 pupils wear glasses. How many pupils are in the two classes altogether?

title: A fraction before and after the refill
prompt: A jug starts with 90 mL. A third of the liquid is poured out, then 15 mL is poured back in. What fraction of the original amount is now in the jug?

title: Two shares of the same original
prompt: On Monday a shop sold one-fifth of its opening stock of cards. On Tuesday it sold one-third of what was then left. It sold 12 more cards on Tuesday than Monday. How many cards did it have when it opened on Monday?

title: The base of the discount
prompt: A jacket's price drops from $80 to $68. By what percentage of its original price was it reduced? Enter the percentage as a number.

title: The exchange of price tags
prompt: Two shirts cost $48 and $72. The cheaper shirt goes up by 25%, and the dearer shirt comes down by 25%. What is the difference between their new prices, in dollars?

title: First a tray, then part of what is left
prompt: A baker puts 12 buns on a tray, then puts half of the buns still in the kitchen on a second tray. There are 15 buns still in the kitchen. How many buns were there before either tray was filled?

title: The two tanks after draining
prompt: Tank A and tank B each hold the same amount of water. One-quarter of the water in A is drained, and two-thirds of the water in B is drained. There are then 25 more litres in A than in B. How many litres did either tank hold at the start?

title: Two groups with one unknown total
prompt: Forty pupils are split between two activities. Half the pupils in music and a quarter of those in art make a poster. Six of the art pupils make a poster. How many posters are made in total if each of these pupils makes one?

title: Part of a tray is moved
prompt: One tray has 12 red and 8 blue tiles. A second has 4 red and 16 blue tiles. Six red tiles are moved from the first tray to the second. What fraction of the tiles in the second tray are now red?

title: A tray of mismatched fractions
prompt: There are 36 biscuits on a tray. Half are plain. Of the biscuits that are not plain, one-third have icing. How many are neither plain nor iced?

title: One-quarter of the loan comes back
prompt: A library lends out two-fifths of its puzzles. The next day, borrowers return one-quarter of the puzzles that were lent out. There are now 63 puzzles in the library. How many puzzles were there before any were lent out?

title: The part of a part of a roll
prompt: A baker has 80 stickers. She uses one-quarter on boxes. She then puts half of the remaining stickers on bags and gives away one-fifth of what is left. How many stickers does she keep?

title: Three ways to reserve a room
prompt: A club gives one-third of its meeting slots to music and then half of what remains to drama. It gives six more slots to chess, leaving 13 unassigned. How many slots were there altogether?

title: An equal share of hats
prompt: Twenty-four people are in a room. Two-thirds of them are wearing hats. How many people without hats must enter so that exactly half of everyone in the room wears a hat?

title: A fraction of a mixed audience
prompt: There are 48 people at a show. A third of the adults and three-quarters of the children arrive early. Exactly 26 people arrive early. How many children are at the show?

title: Return to three quarters
prompt: A bottle was full. When one-third of its contents was poured out, 12 mL was poured back in. The bottle then held three-quarters of its capacity. What is its full capacity in millilitres?

title: Compare two orderings of the same cuts
prompt: A strip of ribbon is cut in two ways. Method A removes 12 cm and then half of what is left. Method B removes half first and then 12 cm. Method A leaves 18 cm. How many centimetres does method B leave?

title: Same final price
prompt: Two lamps have the same sale price. The first had an original price of $72 and was reduced by 25%. The second was reduced by 10%. What was the second lamp's original price in dollars?

title: The discount is counted on a different price
prompt: A shop offers either 30% off a set of markers, or 20% off followed by a further $6 off. Both offers give the same price. What is the original price, in dollars?
